posts.title: PlotPickle.com now follows the source
posts.author: Bryan Elgin Harris
posts.summary: PlotPickle.com is moving to a GitHub-governed publishing model: source first, verified build second, Human publish last.

sections.heading: One source of truth
paragraphs: PlotPickle is built in the open. The public site should work the same way.

The PlotPickle repository is now the governing source for public copy, public assets, Blog posts and discovery metadata. ChatGPT Sites remains the hosting and publication surface rather than a separate editorial source.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A public page should be traceable to the code and content that produced it. That makes changes reviewable, reversible and easier to keep aligned with the product itself.
The publication boundary remains Human-controlled: a reviewed GitHub change can produce a deployable Site version, but publication is still a deliberate decision.

posts.title: OSS Radar: learning from the open-source frontier
posts.author: Bryan Elgin Harris
posts.summary: PlotPickle's OSS Radar watches open-source story, agent, visual-production and local-AI work for transferable ideas rather than chasing trends.

sections.heading: What the Radar does
paragraphs: OSS Radar scans open-source work for ideas that could save PlotPickle work, strengthen an existing system, reveal a missing capability or teach us something useful.

The internal report is broader and more technical than the public Blog. Public Radar posts are a separate editorial projection: useful projects, factual links and the transferable lesson, without exposing internal implementation scoring or private roadmap reasoning.

sections.heading: Human review stays in the loop
paragraphs: A repository appearing in OSS Radar does not authorize an installation, dependency change or product rewrite.
The Radar may generate a public Blog draft, but a Human must review the article and merge the GitHub change before it can become part of PlotPickle.com.

posts.title: OSS Radar: September 2026, by date
posts.author: Bryan Elgin Harris
posts.summary: A dated public index of PlotPickle's September OSS Radar reports, preserving Human review between discovery and adoption.

sections.heading: How to read the Radar
paragraphs: Each date below records projects surfaced for Human review. Inclusion is a research signal, not an installation, endorsement, dependency decision or promise that a capability will enter PlotPickle.
The full GitHub reports contain the deterministic discovery evidence. This Blog entry is the public, date-ordered index.

sections.heading: September 20, 2026
paragraphs: The public digest highlighted awesome-ai-storyboarding, viforge, moshu, Mana, anamnesis, LocalLLMServerManager and agmi across interface, orchestration, local-AI, memory, provider-runtime and validation concerns.
The strongest shared question was how a local-first story system can connect creative surfaces, bounded agents, durable context and operational evidence without locking itself to one provider.

sections.heading: September 19, 2026
paragraphs: The public digest highlighted CopilotKit, WeKnora, cycgraph, OpenViking, saga, sekai-chisei and NyxID.
Together they offered review material around generative interfaces, knowledge retrieval, context compression, agent memory, story graphs, governed local control and secure API access.

sections.heading: September 18, 2026
paragraphs: The public digest highlighted OpenUI, story-skills, wind-comic, design-os-3d-blender, ideagraph-live, mnemos and agentguard.
The day connected generative UI, story-writing skills, multi-agent visual production, tool execution, persistent idea graphs, interoperable memory and agent safeguards.

sections.heading: September 17, 2026
paragraphs: The review queue highlighted cinedrama-os, clawdius, agent-kernel, mcp-context-forge and saga.
The recurring themes were storyboard-to-production flow, safer execution, scalable agent orchestration, centralized tool gateways and story systems built around persistent knowledge.

sections.heading: September 16, 2026
paragraphs: The review queue highlighted cinedrama-os, clawdius, agent-kernel, mcp-context-forge and saga.
These were retained as research candidates for visual production, sandboxed execution, orchestration, MCP interoperability and knowledge-graph-supported writing.

sections.heading: September 15, 2026
paragraphs: The review queue highlighted drama-skills, agent-kernel, cinedrama-os, awesome-ai-storyboarding and SST.
The useful comparison points ranged from reusable dramatic-writing skills and agent infrastructure to cinematic production systems and script-to-visual workflows.

sections.heading: September 14, 2026
paragraphs: The review queue highlighted openamer, Nexus-Hub, agent-kernel, clawdius and cinedrama-os.
The report kept the focus on inspectable approaches to agent workbenches, coordination, governed execution and visual-production pipelines.

sections.heading: September 13, 2026
paragraphs: The first September report highlighted narrative-soundstage, visual-ui-debug-agent-mcp, VAIXLNS, testzeus-hercules and Orkas.
The initial review set covered script performance, visual interface debugging, architecture ideas, agent testing and orchestration.

sections.heading: Human review remains the publication boundary
paragraphs: OSS Radar may prepare discovery evidence and a public draft. A Human still decides what is accurate, useful and appropriate to publish.
No Radar entry can install software, change PlotPickle architecture, alter curriculum or authorize product work on its own.
